name: Early rice farmers of mainland Southeast Asia
summary: Rice-farming and bronze-working peoples of Thailand, Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia, known from sites such as Ban Chiang and the Đông Sơn culture, ancestors of later Southeast Asian kingdoms.

knownFor.label: Đông Sơn drums
knownFor.note: Large decorated bronze drums from northern Vietnam.

knownFor.label: Ban Chiang pottery
knownFor.note: Pottery painted with red swirls, from north-east Thailand.

location.value: Northeast Thailand: Ban Chiang, in Nong Han district, Udon Thani province.

terrain.value: River valleys (Mekong, Red River) and plains.
terrain.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

climate.value: Tropical monsoon climate: a hot wet season from about May to October that flooded rice fields, followed by a dry season.
climate.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

resources.value: Rice, fish and shellfish, forest animals, and copper and tin ores in Laos and Thailand, mined at sites such as Phu Lon and Khao Wong Prachan.
resources.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

disasters.value: Probably river floods and droughts, though archaeology gives little direct evidence.
disasters.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

population.value: The article gives no population estimate.

urbanisation.value: Villages; some larger settlements by the end.
urbanisation.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

disease.value: Little known; skeletons from Ban Chiang and Khok Phanom Di show early deaths, anaemia and other health stresses.
disease.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

migration.value: Rice farmers moved south from southern China.
migration.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

economicBase.value: Rice farming, fishing, raising pigs, cattle and chickens, and making pottery and bronze tools, as at Ban Chiang and Non Nok Tha.
economicBase.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

tradeRoutes.value: Exchange of bronze drums across the region.
tradeRoutes.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

wealth.value: No estimate is possible; burials with bronze, shell and stone ornaments suggest some families had more than others.
wealth.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

moneyAndTax.value: No money or taxes; goods such as shell beads, bronze and salt were probably exchanged between villages.
moneyAndTax.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

inequality.value: Some graves, such as the rich “Princess” burial at Khok Phanom Di with thousands of shell beads, held far more goods than others.
inequality.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

governmentType.value: Small villages; the article describes villages only, not chiefdoms.

keyRulers.value: No rulers are known by name, as there was no writing; rich Đông Sơn burials with bronze drums may belong to chiefs late in the period.
keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

succession.value: Unknown; leadership was probably based on family, age and wealth within village communities.
succession.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

institutions.value: Unknown; villages probably ran their own affairs through family and community leaders.
institutions.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

stability.value: Unknown, but some villages, such as Ban Chiang, were lived in for many centuries, suggesting long stability.
stability.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

eliteConflict.value: Unknown; there is no clear evidence of conflict between elites until late in the period.
eliteConflict.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

armyAndTech.value: Bronze axes, spearheads and daggers appear in the Đông Sơn period, alongside the first iron weapons.
armyAndTech.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

majorWars.value: No wars are known; moated settlements in north-east Thailand appear near the end of the period.
majorWars.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

territoryChange.value: Rice farming spread from southern China into the river valleys of Vietnam, Thailand, Laos and Cambodia after about 2500 BCE.
territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

alliancesRivals.value: Unknown; the spread of bronze drums and shell ornaments shows contact between distant communities.
alliancesRivals.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

inventions.value: Bronze casting (from about 1500 BCE), later iron.
inventions.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

scienceEducation.value: No writing; skills such as rice farming, pottery and bronze casting were passed on by practice and example.
scienceEducation.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

openness.value: Fairly open: bronze drums and stone beads travelled widely, and by the end there was trade with India and China.
openness.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

communicationTransport.value: Dugout boats on rivers and along the coast, and footpaths between villages.
communicationTransport.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

religion.value: Unknown; burials with goods suggest belief in an afterlife.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

languageWriting.value: No writing; people probably spoke early Austroasiatic languages (ancestors of Mon, Khmer and Vietnamese), with Tai–Kadai speakers to the north.
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

artsArchitecture.value: Ban Chiang’s red-painted pottery with swirling designs, and Đông Sơn bronze drums decorated with boats, birds and dancers.
artsArchitecture.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

socialStructure.value: Village communities with emerging chiefs; rich graves suggest leading families, especially in the later bronze and iron periods.
socialStructure.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

sharedIdentity.value: Unknown; shared pottery styles and burial customs suggest regional cultures such as Ban Chiang and Đông Sơn.
sharedIdentity.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

dailyLife.value: Families probably lived in wooden houses on stilts, grew rice, fished, kept pigs and chickens, and buried the dead with pots and ornaments.
dailyLife.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

neighbours.value: Farming peoples of southern China to the north, and Austronesian seafarers along the coasts and islands to the south and east.
neighbours.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

ideasReligions.value: Indian influence, including Hinduism and Buddhism, arrived only after this period, with early states such as Funan.
ideasReligions.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

colonisation.value: No colonisation in the later sense; farming spread through migration and contact rather than conquest by a state.
colonisation.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

riseSignals.value: Bronze making began around 2000 BCE by radiocarbon dating; rice from about 2100 BCE. Higham’s bone-based date for settlement is about 1500 BCE, so the dating is disputed.

peakPeriod.value: The Đông Sơn culture (about 1000 BCE–100 CE).
peakPeriod.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

declineSignals.value: Not a decline: chiefdoms grew into early states.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

outcome.value: Followed by Funan, Champa and other states.
outcome.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

sources.value: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture.
sources.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture

overallCertainty.source: Wikipedia: Ban Chiang; Wikipedia: Đông Sơn culture
